title: The King and the Chamberlain's Virtuous Wife

keywords: tale of the king and his chamberlain's wife
full_text:
King Shahriman of ancient Persia was inspecting the residential quarters of his capital when he stopped before the house of his chief chamberlain, seeking a glass of sherbet. The chamberlain’s wife, a lady of celebrated modesty and intellect, received her sovereign with serene dignity, served him the iced drink from behind the silk curtain, and spoke with refined eloquence.

The king, momentarily tempted by selfish impulse, lingered in the courtyard.

The noble lady smiled with calm majesty and recited an ancient parable: 'Sire, if an imperial eagle soaring in the azure sky swoops down to take the humble sparrow’s nest, the world will not praise his valor; they will say: "The king of birds has forgotten his majesty to plunder the straw of the weak!"'

The words pierced King Shahriman’s conscience like an arrow. Filled with shame, he bowed his head, left his gold signet ring upon the table as an offering of reverence for her virtue, and departed without uttering another word.

When the chamberlain returned, he found the royal ring and was troubled by dark doubts.

The king summoned the chamberlain before the full council, promoted him to Grand Chancellor, and declared before all the emirs: 'Your garden was visited by the King, but its walls were guarded by angels of honor that no monarch could ever cross!'

The household lived in honored peace, having conquered temptation through moral courage and poetic wit.
moral: A monarch’s honor is proven by respecting the domestic peace of his loyal servants.
